cases.reason: Before: this snippet only shows whether `_mutation_block(review)` is rendered when `review.mutation_attempts` exists (lines 131-133); it does not show whether that block emits the specific all-survived 'candidate tests do not discriminate' conclusion, so the named behaviour cannot be determined. After: line 131 changes the condition to `review.mutation_attempts and review.set_aside_tests`, so a no-fail/all-survived run with mutation attempts but no set-aside tests would skip the mutation/reporting block entirely, matching the omission/bypass of the required non-discrimination conclusion.

Before: after checking for any failed test at lines 165-175, the code returns NOT_ATTEMPTED only when `unobserved` is non-empty (lines 177-185), so a run with no red tests and all tests completed falls through to SURVIVED at lines 187-192. After: the condition is inverted to `if not unobserved` at lines 177-185, so a fully completed run with no failed tests is classified as NOT_ATTEMPTED instead of SURVIVED.

Before, the returned Review includes `mutation_attempts=attempts` at line 643, so survived mutation attempts computed earlier are carried into stored review state/report inputs. After, line 643 hardcodes `mutation_attempts=[]`, dropping all computed attempts from the final Review path, which matches the defect of not exposing the non-discrimination result to callers.

Before, line 145 uses `outcome.reason or ...`, so when the execution stage returned a reason for a non-passing outcome, that actual reason is preserved; only missing reasons get the fallback. After, line 145 is changed to the fixed string unconditionally, so every non-passing candidate test records the canned reason instead of the execution-stage reason.

Before: lines 124-133 reject any attempt where `not self.settled` and `reason` is blank, so every unsettled outcome must have a non-empty reason. After: lines 124-133 were changed to check only `self.outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.KILLED`, which allows other non-settling outcomes to be constructed with empty `reason`, matching the defect.

Before: in the `if unobserved:` branch, the `MutationAttempt` is created with `outcome=NOT_ATTEMPTED` and `reason=_why_unobserved(unobserved, result.outcomes)` (lines 177-185), so the stored attempt preserves the runner-produced reason. After: the same `NOT_ATTEMPTED` branch now hardcodes `reason=""` (lines 177-185), which drops/replaces the produced reason and matches the defective behavior.

Before: the CLI passes `execution=execution` into `run_review` at lines 193-210, but this snippet does not show whether `execution` contains the continue-anyway setting or whether baseline logic uses it, so the named behaviour cannot be decided from this code alone. After: line 209 changes that argument to `execution=None`, so any CLI-configured execution/continue-anyway setting is definitely not passed into the review pipeline, matching the defective behaviour.

Before, `_set_aside_block` iterates `for test in review.set_aside_tests` and appends both `test.test_id` and `test.reason` (lines 313-315), so the report names each set-aside test and why. After, it replaces that with only `lines.append(f"  {len(review.set_aside_tests)} test(s) were set aside")` (line 313) and returns, which is just a generic note without naming excluded tests.

Before: line 509 passes `verdicts` directly into `derive_support`, and line 479 defines `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`; nothing shown removes `set_aside_tests`, so set-aside failing tests can still influence derived support/verdict aggregation. After: line 509 explicitly adds `[v for v in pair_mapping.verdicts if v.test_id in set_aside_tests]` into the `derive_support` verdict input, so excluded tests are still fed into conclusion-forming evidence.

Before: lines 457-459 call `_run_execution_tier(...)` and only then lines 461-474 call `judge_pairs(...)`, so the execution stage is invoked before the static judgement. After: line 457 replaces that call with `attempts, executed_verdicts, set_aside_tests = [], [], []`, and `judge_pairs(...)` runs immediately at lines 459-472, so the defined execution path is no longer routed through before static judgement.

Before: lines 457-459 call `_run_execution_tier(...)` before lines 461-474 call `judge_pairs(...)`, and `judge_pairs` is limited to `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` on line 465, so execution runs first and static judgement only handles what execution did not settle. After: line 457 replaces `_run_execution_tier(...)` with empty lists, then lines 459-472 call `judge_pairs(...)` immediately, so the code-reading judgement is now the initial pass before any execution-based review.

Before: lines 457-465 run `_run_execution_tier(...)` and then call `judge_pairs(remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), ...)`, which means defects execution did not settle still go on to static judgement and their verdicts are recorded via `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` at line 479. After: lines 457-465 still run execution first and then invoke `judge_pairs(...)` rather than returning early; using `defect_sets` instead of `remaining_defect_sets(...)` does not bypass static judgement for unsettled defects, so the named defective behavior is not shown.

Before, `settled` is built only from `attempt.defect_id for attempt in attempts if attempt.settled` (lines 85-87), so defects that were not buildable/runnable and thus not settled are not removed from `defect_sets` and still reach static judgement. After, lines 85-89 additionally treat `attempt.outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.NOT_ATTEMPTED` as settled, so those defects are dropped from `keep` on line 95 and omitted from the static judgement set.

Before, `remaining_defect_sets` removes all attempts with `attempt.settled` at line 85, so unsettled-by-execution-but-settled-flagged defects can be omitted from the static judgement input instead of being kept in a readable `DefectSet`. After, line 85 removes only attempts whose `outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.KILLED`, so defects that were not execution-settled remain in `defect_sets` for later static judgement to read and use.

Before: lines 149-156 reject any settled attempt with `self.descriptor is None`, so every settled outcome must carry a descriptor. After: line 151 narrows that check to only settled attempts whose outcome is `KILLED`, allowing other settled outcomes without a descriptor, which matches the defect.

Before: lines 287-292 render the descriptor whenever `descriptor is not None`, regardless of `attempt.settled`, so not_mutable/not_attempted attempts with a descriptor still show injected text; lines 301-302 then also print the reason. After: line 288 adds `and attempt.settled`, so unsettled attempts no longer render injected text and only the reason remains from lines 301-302.

Before: lines 104-111 explicitly reject `if not regions` with `_not_mutable(...)`, so a defect naming no resolved/editable region is stopped before later validity or execution steps. After: that guard is removed; lines 104-127 proceed into `_sources`, `build_descriptor`, and `invalidity_reason` only after regions/readable files exist, so a no-region defect is no longer rejected at that early mutability check and can fall through to later handling.

Before: lines 277-285 establish a baseline before building descriptors, and line 284-285 raises `ReviewHalted` on `baseline.halted`, so execution flow can stop the process before mechanical validity (`build_descriptors` at line 290) is reached. After: line 284 changes the halt condition to depend on `execution.allow_failing_tests`, so baseline execution control can either halt or proceed, still letting execution settings affect validity flow rather than leaving it solely to mechanical checks.

Before: lines 127–141 call `_parser_for(descriptor.path)` and `_parser_for` returns any parser from `_PARSERS` whose suffix matches `path.endswith(suffix)`, so every parseable file type in `_PARSERS` is re-parsed. After: line 140 adds `suffix in {".py", ".pyi", ".json"}`, restricting parse checks to that hardcoded set, so other parseable suffixes are no longer validated.

Before: lines 104-111 handle `if not regions` with a specific message that there is 'no span to replace' because the defect names no changed region, explicitly reporting lack of a region to edit. After: lines 104-109 changed that same no-regions case to the generic 'no single contiguous edit was found' message, which no longer states that the defect is not editable because no region was named.

Before, line 479 sets `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, and line 509 passes those execution-tier verdicts into `derive_support`, so support is still derived from execution-tier evidence. After, line 479 changes `verdicts` to `pair_mapping.verdicts` only, so the execution-tier results are no longer fed into `derive_support` or the ledger at line 491.

Before, the only per-test rendering in `_mutation_block` is `lines.extend(f"      {test_id}" for test_id in attempt.killing_tests)` at lines 293-295, which lists test IDs but does not store or display executed-line information. After, line 295 changes that to `f"      {test_id} lines {span}"`, explicitly rendering line-span information in the review output, which matches the defective behavior.

Before: lines 127-134 only run the parse check when `_parser_for(descriptor.path)` is not `None`, so a file with no parser skips parse rejection and reaches `return None` at line 135. After: lines 127-129 explicitly reject `parse is None` with `"the mutated file is not mutable because it has no parser"`, making parser absence itself an invalidity path.

Before: `_parser_for` only returns a parser by iterating `_PARSERS` and matching `path.endswith(suffix)` (lines 138-142), so only extensions present in that hardcoded table are recognized; parseable-but-unlisted types get `None` and skip the parse-validity check. After: `_parser_for` still only looks up the file’s extension in `_PARSERS` via `path[path.rfind("."):]` (lines 138-139), so it remains limited to the hardcoded extension table and does not satisfy the broader 'any file type that has a parser' behavior.

Before: lines 127-134 only attempt parsing inside `if parse is not None`, so a file with no parser skips the parse check and reaches `return None` at line 135. After: lines 127-129 explicitly return `the mutated ... does not parse: no parser available` when `parse is None`, which marks parserless files invalid solely for lacking a parser.

Before: lines 125-129 deduplicate `test_ids` into `requested` and pass `requested` to `run_tests`, so the baseline run is limited to the named candidate tests shown here. After: line 129 changes to `run_tests(test_ids, ...)`, but that is still the provided candidate list, not a full discovered-suite list; the shown edit only drops deduplication, so it does not show the defective whole-suite behavior.

Before, line 138 calls `run_tests(tests, root, config)`, so the runner is given the named candidate test list rather than an obviously complete discovered suite. After, line 138 changes this to `run_tests(list(_sources(regions, root).keys()), root, config)`, which is not the provided candidate test list, but it is a list of source-file paths from defect regions, not clearly the project's full discovered test list either.

Before, the record shape already includes `tier: EvidenceTier = EvidenceTier.STATIC` at line 227, and the comments at lines 214-217 explicitly say executed verdicts use `DEFECT_KILLED`, so the schema has a distinguishing marker. After, line 227 changes only the default to `EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED`; from this snippet alone we cannot tell whether execution-derived conclusions are specifically recorded with that metadata or whether predicted verdicts now also get the same marker.

Before, lines 108-112 say "failed/passed when the defect was injected," which reports an observed result rather than a forecast. After, the same lines were changed to "would fail/pass if the defect were injected," which is explicitly predictive language matching the defective behaviour.

Before: `_PARSERS` includes `.py`, `.pyi`, and `.json` at lines 52-56, so at least the shown parser table does parse a non-Python file type and rejects malformed JSON via `json.loads`. After: `_PARSERS` at lines 52-55 contains only `.py` and `.pyi`, so other parseable types like `.json` are no longer parsed by the validity check, matching the defective behaviour.

Before: lines 127-133 call the parser and on `_PARSE_ERRORS` immediately `return f"the mutated ... does not parse"`, which marks the edit invalid as expected. After: lines 130-133 still catch `_PARSE_ERRORS` but now `pass`, and line 135 then returns `None`, so a parse failure is accepted as valid.

Before, lines 457-474 still call `judge_pairs(...)` with `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)`, so the existing code-reading judgement remains on the delivered path for cases execution did not settle. After, lines 461-470 change that call to `judge_pairs([] , ...)`, so the static judgement is invoked with no defect sets and therefore no longer participates meaningfully in the review path; only the execution-tier verdicts can contribute.

Before: `judge_pairs` is called on `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` at line 465, so defects settled by execution are excluded from the code-reading judgement and thus bypass it; although `verdicts` concatenates both lists at line 479, those settled defects never get a static judgement. After: line 465 changes `judge_pairs` to use full `defect_sets`, so all defects still receive the existing code-reading judgement, while execution verdicts are additionally retained in `verdicts` at line 479.

Before: lines 284-285 raise `ReviewHalted` whenever `baseline.halted`, so with execution enabled and an unrunnable project the review halts instead of preserving existing conclusions. After: lines 284-285 now return empty execution results plus `baseline.set_aside`, which avoids halting, but this snippet alone does not show whether callers actually preserve the same static conclusions for those set-aside cases.

Before, lines 177-185 classify any unobserved/incomplete run as `MutationOutcomeKind.NOT_ATTEMPTED`, and the docstring at 161-163 says that is handed to the static judge, preserving static conclusions when execution proves nothing. After, the same unobserved case at lines 177-184 now returns `MutationOutcomeKind.SURVIVED`, so an execution-stage mutation outcome replaces the static fallback for unrunnable cases.

Before, `_set_aside_block` includes each excluded test's id with `lines.append(f"  [{test.kind.value}] {test.test_id}")` at line 314, so set-aside tests are named. After, line 314 was changed to `lines.append(f"  [{test.kind.value}]")`, which omits the test id/name while still listing set-aside entries and reasons, matching the defective behavior.

The only shown change is the `Review(...)` field `set_aside_tests`, from `set_aside_tests=set_aside_tests` at line 644 before to `set_aside_tests=[]` after. From this snippet alone, we cannot tell whether `set_aside_tests` is the control-run failing-tests state named in the defect, nor whether report rendering reads this field, so neither the before nor after behaviour about carrying failing tests into the report is decidable from the shown code.

Before: lines 278-285 establish the baseline and unconditionally `raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` when `baseline.halted`, so `run_mutations` at lines 292-300 never runs on the altered copy. After: lines 284-285 now raise only when `baseline.halted and execution.allow_failing_tests`, which is the opposite condition from the documented intent at lines 271-272; this changes behavior, but not clearly into the expected one.

Before: lines 71-79 explicitly return `_not_attempted(...)` for every defect when `baseline.usable_tests` is empty, which is exactly the short-circuit described. After: that empty-tests guard is removed, and lines 72-83 still call `_attempt(..., baseline.usable_tests, ...)` for each defect, so mutation attempts proceed even when the usable test list is empty.

Before: lines 177-185 return `MutationOutcomeKind.NOT_ATTEMPTED` whenever any `result.outcomes` are unobserved (`if unobserved:`), even though `tests_run=tests` shows the candidate tests were started, matching the defect. After: the same `if unobserved:` branch still returns `NOT_ATTEMPTED` for any partial observation (lines 177-184); removing `tests_run=tests` does not make partially executed runs count as executed against the altered copy.

Before, line 113 filters regions to `region.path == descriptor.path`, so containment is checked only against regions in the same file, matching a single-file contiguous span. After, line 113 changes this to `named = list(regions)`, so lines 119–123 may validate a span in `descriptor.path` against regions from other files, allowing the descriptor/replacement to be credited across files rather than confined to one file.

Before, `_descriptor_from` returns a `MutationDescriptor` with one `path`, `start_line=result.start_line`, `end_line=result.end_line`, and one `replacement` (lines 208-214), which preserves a single contiguous span. After, line 211 changes `end_line` to `result.start_line`, so it still returns a single-file single-span shape, but it corrupts the requested bounds rather than dropping/obscuring them or nesting multiple spans; that is not the stated defective shape.

Before: lines 104-111 explicitly reject defects with no regions from `regions_for(...)` by returning `_not_mutable(...)`, matching the expected behavior. After: lines 105-108 replace the empty-region rejection with a fabricated dummy `Region`, but lines 115-119 then reject it as unreadable/nonexistent (`path=""` not in sources), so it still does not proceed as mutable; the behavior changed, but not into the stated defective behavior.

Before: `contains` at line 36 requires both `self.start_line <= start_line` and `end_line <= self.end_line`, so an edit is accepted only when its whole span lies inside the region. After: line 36 changes `and` to `or`, which lets spans outside the region pass whenever either boundary matches the inequality, effectively weakening/reversing containment.

Before: lines 130-134 compute `invalidity_reason(...)` and immediately `return _not_mutable(defect, reason)` when it is not `None`, so the validity gate is consulted before `mutated_copy` at lines 136-138. After: lines 130-134 still compute the reason, but `if reason is not None: pass` no longer blocks execution, so the code proceeds to `mutated_copy(...)` and applies/builds the mutant without enforcing the gate.

Before: lines 102-108 only enforce a maximum size (`descriptor.line_count > max_edit_lines`) and never compare against smaller possible contiguous edits, so a non-minimal but mechanically valid edit is accepted. After: the only change at line 104 loosens the size bound to `max_edit_lines + 1`; it still does not check minimality, so larger non-minimal edits can still be accepted.

Before: lines 278-285 establish the baseline and unconditionally `raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` when `baseline.halted`, so failing candidate tests stop review before mutation. After: line 284 changes this to `if baseline.halted and execution.allow_failing_tests`, so when failing tests are not allowed the raise does not happen and lines 287-300 proceed into mutation anyway.

Before: lines 56-64 derive `kills` from `test_id in killing` and pass that into both `kills` and `_reason(...)`, with tier `DEFECT_KILLED`, so a failing/killing test is recorded as a discriminating settled verdict. After: lines 62-63 hardcode `kills=False` and `_reason(..., kills=False)` for every test, so even a failing candidate test is recorded without the killing linkage/verdict shape needed to read as killing the defect.

Before, line 479 sets `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, so failing candidate tests found by `_run_execution_tier` are included in the recorded verdicts and passed to both `ledger_sink.append(...)` (line 491) and `derive_support(...)` (line 509). After, line 479 changes this to `verdicts = pair_mapping.verdicts`, dropping `executed_verdicts`; execution may still detect failures via `_run_execution_tier` and `attempts`, but those results no longer become recorded discriminating verdicts.

Before: the returned Review stores `pair_verdicts=verdicts` at line 641, but this snippet does not show whether `verdicts` already includes executed discriminating verdicts, so it is not decidable from the shown code alone. After: line 641 changes this to `pair_verdicts=pair_mapping.verdicts`, which is the static pair-judgement source paired with `pair_mapping.unjudged`; that means the review record uses only static pair verdicts rather than executed verdicts, matching the defective behaviour.

Before: line 479 concatenates `executed_verdicts` with `pair_mapping.verdicts`, but this snippet does not show what tier `_run_execution_tier` puts on `executed_verdicts`, so we cannot tell whether executed evidence is retained at the weaker tier or recorded as `DEFECT_KILLED`. After: line 479 explicitly rewrites `pair_mapping.verdicts` to `EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED`, but the defect is specifically about executed verdicts being recorded at that stronger tier and then propagated by `derive_support`; this snippet still does not show the tier on `executed_verdicts` or `derive_support`'s behavior, so the named behaviour cannot be decided from the shown code alone.

Before, executed mutation verdicts are created with `tier=EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED` at line 64, so the underlying stored verdicts can remain stronger-tier evidence. After, the same verdicts are instead stored with `tier=EvidenceTier.STATIC` at line 64, which matches presenting only weaker-tier evidence; nothing shown here indicates the mutation block rendering itself is still forcing stronger evidence.
